title: Validate a snapshot
description:
Write `problems(snapshot, previousFrame)`, which checks a telemetry snapshot from Delve and returns a list of problem names, in this order, for each check that fails:

| Check | Problem name |
|---|---|
| `magic` is `0x54564C44` | `"magic"` |
| `version` is 1 | `"version"` |
| `size` is at least 48 | `"size"` |
| `frame` is not less than `previousFrame` | `"frame went backwards"` |
| `frameMs` is greater than 0 and less than 10000 | `"frame time"` |
| `floor` is between 1 and 99 | `"floor"` |
| `playerMaxHp` is between 1 and 10000, and `playerHp` between 0 and `playerMaxHp` | `"health"` |
| `monstersAlive` is between 0 and 10000 | `"monsters"` |

If the magic number is wrong, return only `{ "magic" }`: nothing else in the block can be trusted. An empty list means the snapshot is valid. Remember that `frameMs` could be NaN (not a number): it must fail the check.
hints: Check the magic first and return straight away if it is wrong. Then run each check in the table's order, pushing its name when it fails.
Write the frame-time check as "not (greater than 0 and less than 10000)". Every comparison with NaN is false, so NaN fails it automatically.
